correctness.rationale: After the orthogonal change \(u=(x+y)/\sqrt2\), \(v=(x-y)/\sqrt2\), the norm satisfies \(N(u,v)^2=u^2+v^2\) when \(|u|\ge|v|\) and \(N(u,v)^2=2v^2\) when \(|v|\ge|u|\). Averaging any quadratic pullback under the coordinate-swap isometry reduces without loss to \(u^2+t v^2\). The two sector ratios have only endpoint extrema, giving the displayed piecewise distortion and unique minimum \(3/2\) at \(t=2\). The same coordinates also show directly that the norm is the Banaś--Frączek norm \(\max\{\sqrt2|v|,\sqrt{u^2+v^2}\}\) after swapping coordinates, providing an independent correctness check.

The present Day--James plane is linearly isometric to the \(\lambda=\sqrt2\) member: in the displayed \((u,v)\) coordinates its norm is exactly \(\max\{\sqrt2|v|,\sqrt{u^2+v^2}\}\). Setting \(\lambda=\sqrt2\) gives \(3/2\), and the published optimal ellipse becomes, up to scale, \(u^2+2v^2\). Thus the entire scientific claim is a direct special case of stronger current published coverage.
